new_statements.rule_in_words: Main (primary) word stress falls on the first syllable of the word in the Goldfields Aboriginal languages (a set that explicitly includes Tjupan); stated as a near-exceptionless generalisation ('almost always'), contrasted with lexical stress in Standard Australian English.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the hedge 'almost always'; no exceptions listed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement in an orthography/pronunciation guide; generic across ~15 Goldfields languages (mostly Western Desert dialects plus Ngadju, Mirniny, Kaalamaya, Warlpiri), not a Tjupan-specific analysis; no data or examples given for stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog's pini1245 'Lake Carnegie Western Desert' conflates Tindale's 'Pini' (retired ISO [pii], AUSTLANG A25 Birniridjara, unconfirmed) with Tjupan/Tjupany ([tjp], AUSTLANG A31), the variety actually documented by GALCAC (speakers around Wiluna/Leonora/Darlot-Carnegie-Wongawol). The quoted statement is NOT Tjupan-specific: it is a group-level generalisation over all 'Goldfields Aboriginal languages' in a GALCAC orthography guide whose scope explicitly includes Tjupan (Tjupan alphabet, p.24). Kuwarra (A16), once listed as a Tjupan synonym, is treated by GALCAC as a separate dialect.
